Given the plots of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ above, find ${h}^{′}(2)$ where $h(x)=\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}.$
question.worked_solution:
The quotient rule for derivatives gives

$$
{h}^{′}(x)=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)\cdot g(x)-f(x)\cdot {g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(2)=\frac{{f}^{′}(2)\cdot g(2)-f(2)\cdot {g}^{′}(2)}{(g(2))^{2}}.
$$

From the graph above, we obtain that $f(2)=\frac{3}{2}$ and $g(2)=-1.$

Additionally:

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (1,3)$ equals $-\frac{1}{2}.$ So, ${f}^{′}(2)=-\frac{1}{2}.$

- The slope of $g(x)$ on $x\in (1,3)$ equals $0.$ So, ${g}^{′}(2)=0.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(2) & =\frac{{f}^{′}(2)\cdot g(2)-f(2)\cdot {g}^{′}(2)}{(g(2))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{1}{2})\cdot (-1)-\frac{3}{2}\cdot 0}{(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{1}{2})}{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
